candidates.name: Amos Rex
candidates.price: General admission €20, reduced €15, students and youth under 30 years €5, children under 18 years free
candidates.hours: Mon 11–20; Wed–Fri 11–20; Sat/Sun 11–17, closed on Tue
candidates.content: A modern arts museum that tends towards immersive, often audiovisual installations and has rapidly gained in acknowledgement since its opening in 2018. While entrance and shop are in Lasipalatsi, the actual museum is a piece archi

candidates.name: Lutheran Cathedral
candidates.price: Jun-Aug 10€ (13€ for a pass including entry to Suomenlinna church and St. John's church as well), Sep-Oct 8€, Nov-May free (8€ voluntary fee)
candidates.content: The unofficial symbol of the city, this striking white cathedral dominates the central Senate Square. Based on designs by Carl Ludvig Engel and completed in 1852, the cathedral has been refurbished, and the 12 Apostles are on the

candidates.name: Uspenski Cathedral
candidates.content: A classical and prominent onion-domed Russian church, the largest Orthodox church in Western Europe, Uspenski Cathedral serves Finland's small Orthodox minority. The name comes from the Russian uspenie, from the Dormition (death)

candidates.name: Helsinki City Museum
candidates.content: The museum covers a whole series of old buildings around Helsinki, but the centrepiece is the (short) street of Sofiankatu itself, carefully restored as a replica of the 1930s.

candidates.name: Ehrensvärd Museum
candidates.content: The first occupant of the current museum building was Augustin Ehrensvärd (1710-1772), the founder of the Suomenlinna fortress. The museum's collection includes paintings, furniture, weapons and ship models.

candidates.name: Military Museum Manege
candidates.hours: Summer opening 12 May-31 Aug (but closed 19-21 Jun) daily 11:00-18:00
candidates.content: Founded in 1929, the central museum of the Finnish Defence Forces. Exhibits vehicles and armament used by Finnish forces during the Winter War and World War II.

candidates.name: National Museum of Finland
candidates.price: €16/11 adult/child. Free admission for visitors under 18. Tuesday has free admission 17:30–20:00
candidates.content: A beautiful classical building houses this old museum, which has been renovated. The exhibit includes displays of artefacts and items relating to Finland's history. Closed until spring 2027.

candidates.name: Urho Kekkonen Museum Tamminiemi
candidates.content: If you are visiting Seurasaari you can also take look into the daily life of Finland's long time president, Urho Kekkonen. His residence Tamminiemi was turned into a museum in the 1980s.

candidates.name: Dirdrichsen Art Gallery
candidates.content: A collection of more than one thousand pieces of Finnish and modern international art, and artifacts from ancient Oriental and Pre-Columbian cultures. It is housed in a modernist building by famed Finnish architect Viljo Revell. G

candidates.name: The Church in the Rock
candidates.hours: Daily 10:00-17:00, but if services or other activities (e.g. weddings) take place the church has limited access for tourist visitors. Phone +358 (0)9 2340 5940 for a bulletin on current activities. English services on Sundays at 14:00, open to the public
candidates.content: An atmospheric of minimalistic church, this church was literally dug out of solid rock. From above, it resembles a crashed UFO. The roof is made of 22 km of copper strips. Completed in 1969, this has become one of Helsinki's

candidates.name: Finlandia Hall
candidates.content: Designed by Finland's best known architect Alvar Aalto. It is across the street from the National Museum. The marble Finlandia Hall is a popular congress and concert venue in Helsinki. The building itself is worth a visit particul

candidates.name: Lasipalatsi
candidates.content: Another of Helsinki's most iconic functionalist buildings right next to Mannerheimintie, the "glass palace" by Viljo Revell, Heimo Riihimäki and Niilo Kokko was finished in 1936 and is functionalist both on the inside and outside.

candidates.name: Finnish Military Museum
candidates.content: Founded in 1929, the central museum of the Finnish Defence Forces.

candidates.name: Seurasaari Open Air Museum
candidates.content: A pleasant little island to the north of the centre, filled with walking trails and a living history museum of authentic old Finnish houses collected from all over the country. An excellent half-day trip, especially in the summer,

candidates.name: Finnish Museum of Natural History
candidates.content: The museum of natural history is operated by Helsinki University and shows Finnish wildlife, dinosaur skeletons and everything in-between.

candidates.name: Villa Gyllenberg
candidates.content: A private art gallery on Kuusisaari island with sculptures and older and contemporary Finnish art.

candidates.name: Hietaniemi Cemetery
candidates.content: Helsinki's equivalent to Arlington in Washington D.C., Hietaniemi is the final resting place for many Finns of importance during the last 200 years: politicians including almost all heads of state, artists and other cultural perso

candidates.name: Olympic Stadium
candidates.content: It was built for the Olympics and renovated for the 2005 World Athletic Championships. In the stadium building you can visit the Sports Museum with medals and other paraphernalia related to sport. Another stadium, the Sonera stadi

candidates.name: Ursa Observatory
candidates.price: €5 for adults, €2 for under age of 16; free for members
candidates.content: The 1926 yellow-coloured observatory, operated by the Astronomical Association Ursa, is still in active use by both members and other enthusiasts, but non-members can also attend public shows to either observe solar phenomena or l

candidates.name: Ateneum Art Museum
candidates.price: Adults €6, under 18 free, special prices may apply during major exhibitions. First Wednesday of the month 17:00–20:00 free admission
candidates.hours: Tue–Fri 09:00–18:00, Wed Thu 09:00–20:00, Sat Sun 11:00–17:00, closed on Mondays
candidates.content: Ateneum can be considered the most nationally significant art museum, and it has the largest collection of paintings and sculptures in Finland. Particularly notable is the collection of works by major Finnish artists. Works includ

candidates.name: Kiasma Museum of Contemporary Art
candidates.price: €7 for adults, €5 for undergraduate students, senior citizens, visual artists, and groups with at least 7 people. Free admission for visitors under 18. First Friday of the month is free
candidates.content: The sometimes unusual collections mostly include works by contemporary Finnish artists and artists from nearby countries. There are also periodical exhibitions. The building is a work of art.

candidates.name: Main post office
candidates.content: Across Mannerheimintie from Lasipalatsi is Helsinki's former main post office, designed by Jorma Järvi, Erik Lindroos and Kaarlo Borg and finished in 1938. However, it hasn't been the main post building since the late 1990s, but h

candidates.name: Metsätalo
candidates.content: This university building has been described as having both functionalist and classicist elements. It was designed by Jussi Paatela, finished in 1939 and its first users were the State Forest Research Institute (Metsätutkimuslaitos

candidates.name: Korkeasaari
candidates.hours: Every day except Christmas Eve: 10:00-20:00, may operate shorter hours on holidays
candidates.content: Helsinki's zoo, with approximately 150 different animal species. The zoos signature animals are the bears, the free-roaming peafowls and the cats (from tigers and lions to European wildcats). Another highlight is Amazonia, a partl

candidates.name: Church of Kallio
candidates.content: On top of the hill at the end of Siltasaarenkatu. The church is built of grey granite (1912) and its massive looks dominate the view from Hakaniemi. It was designed by Finnish architect Lars Sonck. The church has both baroque and

candidates.name: Worker Housing Museum
candidates.content: Built for the city's employees and their families in the early 20th century, nowadays the house is a museum where every room is a snapshot of the inhabitants' everyday life during different decades from the 1920s to the 1980s. Vis

candidates.name: Torkkelinmäki
candidates.content: The green parks and small apartment buildings on the top of a hill and in the center of Finland's densest-populated neighbourhood are protected as an exemplary early-20th century working-class cultural environment. Around, you wil

candidates.name: Helsinki synagogue
candidates.content: The centre of the Jewish community in Helsinki; there are also a Jewish school, kindergarten and a kosher store on the premises. You probably have to call ahead for visiting.

candidates.name: Helsinki International Film Festival
candidates.content: Also known as Rakkautta & Anarkiaa (Love & Anarchy) and held annually in September, HIFF features a wide selection of films from all over the world. Asian films have been a special focus in the history of the festival that began i

candidates.name: Baltic Herring Market
candidates.content: Taking place in early October, the event sees a large number of islanders arriving at Helsinki's South Harbour to sell fish and other archipelago products. The event has been held since 1743.

candidates.name: Kotiharjun sauna
candidates.price: €12 for adults, students & pensioners €8.5, towel €3 extra.
candidates.content: This is the last wood-burning public sauna in Helsinki. Separate saunas for men and women. There's a good chance you'll find a top level chess match in the dressing room. Don't miss cooling off outside, especially in winter. On Sa

candidates.name: Kulttuuritalo
candidates.content: The Helsinki Hall of Culture is a concert hall designed by Alvar Aalto in the 1950s, and part of the Aalto Works . Since its opening, many world-famous artists and groups such as Jimi Hendrix, AC/DC, Tina Turner, Iron Maiden and L

candidates.name: Suvilahti
candidates.content: A former power plant, nowadays a centre for alternative culture that hosts a circus and some exhibitions. The famous metal festival Tuska at the turn of June and July and electronic music festival Flow in August are held on the pr

candidates.name: Suvilahti DIY
candidates.content: A popular skatepark built by the skaters themselves. The place has even been used by many internationally famous skaters, such as Tony Hawk. It has been under threat since 2017, losing an appeal in 2024.

candidates.name: Tokoinranta
candidates.content: A park north-west of Hakaniemi, which in August turns into an outdoor scene during the Helsingin Juhlaviikot cultural festival. Check out the City theatre, and if you understand Finnish or Swedish, go see a theatre performance.

candidates.name: Brahenkenttä
candidates.content: An open sports pitch in northern Kallio where you can play football (soccer) in the summer and ice hockey or bandy in the winter or watch a home game of the Finnish bandy league team HIFK.

candidates.name: Mäkelänrinne swimming hall
candidates.content: Indoor swimming pool which has also been used for international competitions. Great if you feel like swimming in the winter but don't care for the traditional Finnish "hole in the ice" swimming.

candidates.name: Yrjönkatu swimming hall
candidates.content: An art-deco bath house with historic architecture. Three types of saunas and a swimming pool. Take a sauna and swim in the nude. There are separate days for women and men. Bathing suits are not banned, but almost everyone goes wit

candidates.name: Studium Catholicum
candidates.content: A Catholic cultural center. Dominicans from France founded the Studium in 1949, and the Dominican Order is still responsible for the center's operations. Studium has a library of more than 40,000 books, whose collections focus on

candidates.name: Lux Helsinki
candidates.content: Beginning of January. Lux Helsinki is an annual event of light installations to cheer residents' and visitors' minds during the darkest time of the year. They are on display over several nights. Lux Helsinki can also be enjoyed as

candidates.name: Helsinki Pride
candidates.content: Finland's biggest and most famous LGBT pride event. Held over a week in late June, culminates in a parade and open-air party on Saturday.

candidates.name: Liquorice and salmiak festival
candidates.content: Finns are known for their taste for liquorice flavoured with the salt ammonium chloride, popularly known as salmiak or salmiakki in Finnish, even if many foreigners may find the taste strange and even repulsive at first. Wanha Sat

candidates.name: Helsinki Philharmonic Orchestra
candidates.content: Performances have moved to the Music House, a brand new visually questionable but acoustically excellent concert hall. Tickets €20. On selected Wednesdays you can go see dress rehearsals for as little as €3 per person. The rehears

candidates.name: Skippered Day Sailing
candidates.content: Visit the coastal archipelago on a 35 ft sailboat, for two hours or full day trips with an experienced skipper. Island hopping is also possible.

candidates.name: Vappu
candidates.content: Vappu began as a north European pagan carnival, and is now an excuse for students to wear brightly colored overalls and for everybody to drink vast amounts of alcohol. At 18:00 on April 30, the statue of Havis Amanda at the Market

candidates.name: World Village Festival
candidates.content: An annual multicultural weekend festival in late May. The event is free to all and a meeting place offering tastes of different cultures and surprises from all over the world, music, dance, food, art, market, information. Several

candidates.name: Helsinki-päivä
candidates.content: This is the birthday of the city. It traditionally starts with the mayor's morning coffee and is celebrated throughout the day with a variety of concerts, performances, exhibitions and guided tours around the city. Nowadays specia

candidates.name: Mummotunneli
candidates.content: The "Mummotunneli" ("Grandma tunnel") is a passage between various restaurants in central Helsinki. There are terraces of various restaurants in the passage, staying open well past midnight. The name "Grandma tunnel" comes from th

candidates.name: Lepakkomies
candidates.price: Free entry to bar, but entrance fee for club nights. Beer starting from €4
candidates.content: The name translates to "bat-man" but the place is hardly themed after Batman, instead after bats in general. A large establishment in two floors, the ground floor functioning as your average Kallio pub, the basement as a venue for

candidates.name: Café Ekberg
candidates.content: One of the classic Helsinki cafés and a Bulevardi institution, which was founded in 1852. Was renovated in 2017 and at that lost some of its old flair. Ekberg has two premises right next to each other, with separate entraces. One

candidates.name: A21 Cocktail Lounge
candidates.price: Drinks €7-25, try the Birch Cooler, Blinker or XXX.
candidates.content: A high-priced but incredibly high quality cocktail bar situated in the city center, a few hundred meters from Stockmann's. Generally serves classic cocktail drinks with a twist, but also features several cocktails with a distinctl

candidates.name: Ravintola Wanhakettu
candidates.price: Drinks €3.50-15, try the Karhu III Pint, Salmari or Kolme Leijonaa Malt Whisky.
candidates.content: A journey into traditional Finnish bar culture, where fireside debates and poetry recitals are a common place occurrence in this historical tavern. Frequented by a more intellectual if not boisterous crowd, the common traveler wil

candidates.name: The Tiger
candidates.price: Cover charge €4-8, free entrance before midnight.
candidates.content: Formerly Lux, this is a contestant for the title of Helsinki's classiest mainstream nightclub, with its dress code, stylish decor, relatively high prices and an age limit of 24. Five bars, two spacious terraces, a VIP lounge and s

candidates.name: Vapari
candidates.content: A rather small pub near the eastern tip of the Katajanokka peninsula. Stylish maritime decor. It's right next to a seniors' home, so many seniors come here often. Beer and cider available on tap but don't expect anything fancy.

candidates.name: Ahjo
candidates.content: Named after the forge where the mythical Sampo of the Kalevala was made, this is a slick modern bar-lounge with two sides to it: a pure white space as you enter, with a bar counter and sofas, and a darker back room with nooks and

candidates.name: Molly Malone's
candidates.content: An Irish pub/nightclub near the Central Railway Station. Popular among Finns and tourists alike. Live music every night, superb English-language cover bands most nights, sometimes a DJ later. If you happen to be in Helsinki at St.

candidates.name: Thirsty Scholar
candidates.content: A pub with a spacious inner courtyard terrace in central Helsinki. Several beers and ciders available on tap and in bottles. University students get a discount on drinks on tap.

candidates.name: Vanha ylioppilastalo
candidates.content: A bar/café opposite Stockmann, owned by University of Helsinki's filthy rich students' union. Not very special in the winter, but the rooftop patio in the summer is nice. In the evenings, the club attracts a slightly-over-18 audie

candidates.name: Tokio Karaoke Helsinki
candidates.content: A pretty cool karaoke bar in the city centre. Reasonably priced drinks and a good crowd with a wide selection of songs. A fun atmosphere with agreeable patrons.

candidates.name: Teatteri
candidates.content: A complex featuring a deli, a restaurant, a bar and a night club, all of them trendy and popular among the well-dressed crowd. Check out the aptly named Clock Bar (Kellobaari) downstairs. Closed Sunday.

candidates.name: Hercules Gay Night Club
candidates.content: One of the busiest gay nightclubs in Scandinavia, mainly a 30+ clients, dance floor and 2 bare, good for bare-faced cruising. Entrance free; coat check €2.50 (on special guests nights fees may vary).

candidates.name: Vltava
candidates.content: The best Czech restaurant in Helsinki. Several floors on the premises, the ground floor consisting of a bar, the upper ones of a restaurant. Several Czech beers on tap, and the menu is based on Czech cuisine with copious amounts o

candidates.name: Pronto Central Station
candidates.content: A little, cosy Italian-style restaurant and café located at the Helsinki Central railway station. Pronto is the "little sister" of the larger restaurant Olivia located right next to it. Serves pizza al taglio, focaccia and Italian

candidates.name: Zetor
candidates.content: Tourist restaurant with lots of character and great quality Finnish food. Plenty of old tractors and Finnish memorabilia. At night time Zetor functions as a popular and trendy night club with various funky music both from Finland

candidates.name: Kappeli
candidates.price: Main lunch dishes €14–18, main dinner dishes about €15–36
candidates.content: Traditional Finnish dishes: reindeer, fish, etc. Some of the prices are a bit high, but you should get polite service and well-prepared food with a lovely presentation. Cosy, relaxed, relatively quiet atmosphere (although the rest

candidates.name: Student's restaurant at Arcada
candidates.hours: Food around lunchtime, coffee, sandwich and cakes all day
candidates.content: Like most other university campuses, the Swedish-language polytechnic Arcada has a lunch restaurant operated by Amica. Even if you aren't a student, the prices for lunch are quite cheap.

candidates.name: Pompier
candidates.content: Run by the Volunteer Fire Brigade, this restaurant serves a daily changing buffet of hearty Finnish fare in a cafeteria straight from the 1950s, complete with grim portraits of moustached Hosemasters staring down at you. Pea soup

candidates.name: Faro
candidates.content: A rather nice restaurant and bar located right at the seashore, offering nice views. Serves lunch and à la carte menu. Lunch is affordable, if not quite cheap, but the à la carte menu is a bit on the pricier side. Also functions a

candidates.name: Katajanokan Pizzapalvelu
candidates.content: A typical neighbourhood pizza and kebab restaurant, also serving pasta, hamburgers and Indian cuisine. The food is very good but hardly spectacular. Comparable to more upscale restaurants in the city centre but for cheaper prices.

candidates.name: Zinnkeller
candidates.content: An authentic German restaurant in the middle of Helsinki, owned by a German immigrant family. Claims to be "the only German restaurant in Finland". Spacious with German-style decor. The menu is full of traditional German food with

candidates.name: Juuri
candidates.price: All sapakset €4.3, main dishes €24, lunch sets €7.5–10
candidates.content: Tiny restaurant known for its special Finnish entrées called sapakset (a play on tapas), with roots in Finnish food tradition. Try the cabbage roll with crayfish or the egg cheese with marjoram.

candidates.name: Sea Horse
candidates.content: Established in 1933 as a basic eatery, this joint has slowly become a local legend affectionately known as Sikala ("Pigsty"), and both the decor and the menu are still preserved from the 1950s. A long-time Wallpaper Magazine favou

candidates.name: Saaga
candidates.content: Traditional Lapp food in kitschy Lapp surroundings – reindeer horn chandeliers and the lot – but unlike some of the competition, they don't compromise on food quality. The octolingual menu runs the gamut from smoked elk to bear me

candidates.name: Stockmann
candidates.content: Northern Europe's largest department store. The flagship of Finland's premier department store chain. When Helsinkians meet "under the clock" (kellon alla), they mean the one rotating under the main entrance to Stockmann. Large se

candidates.name: Market Square
candidates.content: At the end of Esplanadi facing the sea, this open-air market sells fresh fish and produce from all over Finland. Open year round. It's busiest in summer, although the Christmas Market in December is also worth a look. One section

candidates.name: Old Market Hall
candidates.content: Next to Market Square, this old brick building houses Finland's best collection of gourmet food boutiques. Try to find the stall which sells beaver sausage.

candidates.name: Kaari
candidates.content: Prisma hypermarket and about 80 other businesses.

candidates.name: Kluuvi
candidates.content: Re-opened after extensive renovations in 2011, the Kluuvi shopping centre features a range of international and domestic brands. Perhaps the most interesting concept is the Eat & Joy Markethall selling organic and local food in th

december.text: Helsinki is among the world's northernmost capitals and the lengthy winter is dark and chilly. Winter temperatures average , but the wind chill and humidity makes it feel even colder and the mercury can plunge below on a particularly cold day. Days are short. In general snow falls only intermittently and often melts in

The tram operates only during the summer (possibly also in the pikkujoulu season before Christmas), running a non-stop sightseeing route with drinks available through the journey. The Junatie metro bridge between Kalasatama and Sörnäinen will be replaced between 2026 and 2028. From May to December in 2027, the metro stations of Sörnäinen, Kalasatama and Kulosaari will be shut down for repairs, temporarily cutting the metro line in half. On weekend nights, intoxicated people wandering around city streets may be an annoyance, especially during summer festivals and on New Year's Eve and April 30, the eve of May Day, which is the most important beer-drinking festival in the Finnish calendar. Warm summer nights always gather a drunken crowd in the centre.

Joulu: In the weeks before Christmas, Aleksanterinkatu is festively lit up, the Christmas lights of the street are ceremonially lit on the last Sunday in November. The open-air Christmas market formerly held in the Esplanadi Park is nowadays held at the Senaatintori (Senate Square). The

New Year's Eve: Like in many other major cities, thousands of Helsinkians gather at Senaatintori next to the Cathedral to welcome the New Year. The event is shown on live television and there is a free outdoor concert as well.

Outdoor Icepark skating: A pair of skates can be rented for an additional fee. The connected café offers the opportunity of defrosting with a cup of hot glögi. There are also dozens of other places to go skating in Helsinki, including outdoor and indoor skating rinks.
Hoplop activity hall for kids: 8-meter-tall adventure maze, slides, cafe.
Outdoor skating Lauttasaari: Two outdoor skating rings, open approximately 2 Jan - 24 Feb, depending on weather.

Tavastia/Semifinal: One of the most prominent rock clubs in Scandinavia, a must see for fans of live rock of any kind. Semifinal has smaller indie/alternative bands for a young crowd. On special nights the two clubs are joined, but usually they host separate gigs. Tickets for all gigs can be bought
